title: Datamatics Global Services Ltd - 532528 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Datamatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore, with EBITDA margin up 343 bps to 19.7%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 101.1 crore at a 19.7% margin, with the margin gain attributed to cost discipline and operational excellence. Digital Operations drove growth (revenue up 16.1%, EBIT margin 19.3%), while Digital Technologies grew 6.1% at an 8.9% EBIT margin and Digital Experiences declined 5.3%. Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance, citing softness from geopolitical uncertainty, and said about 60% of FY27 deals won were AI-led or AI-driven. The TNQTech integration into Lumina Datamatics was completed in the quarter, and a INR 200 crore TNQTech payout was made in Q1.

segments.name: Digital Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 296.8 crore, up 16.1% YoY; EBIT margin 19.3%. TNQTech is integrated here, per management.

segments.name: Digital Technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 153.1 crore, up 6.1% YoY; EBIT margin 8.9%. Carries the company's AI R&D spend of about INR 40-50 crore a year, which management says depresses the margin.

segments.name: Digital Experiences
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 64 crore, down 5.3% YoY; EBIT margin 11.7%. Management said several good-sized deals were signed this year and the practice is seeing an upswing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of high single digits, maintained despite market softness.
Full-year EBITDA margin expected to rise about 0.5 percentage point, to close to 20%; management later said 19-20% at year end.
AI R&D spend to stay at about the same level (INR 40-50 crore) in FY27; FY28 budget not yet decided.

Management cited a roughly 3-year target of about INR 3,000 crore revenue, versus about INR 2,000 crore now, to be a mix of organic and inorganic growth; it was described as starting in the current year.
Annual salary increments effective April 2026 are already reflected in Q1 numbers.
M&A dialogue is ongoing but no deal has matured to disclosure stage.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were discussed.

AI platforms cited as growth drivers: KAiBRE and KAiSDLC for legacy modernisation, KAi underwriting for insurance, agentic claims processing, and SuperCX for contact-centre and front-office automation.
Legacy modernisation projects reportedly compress timelines from about three years to about six months; first underwriting-product revenue has been booked with one customer.
demand_pricing: Customers are choosing Datamatics for AI capability; recent wins include SBI Life Insurance (TruAI underwriting), a US pet and veterinary provider (AI voice agent) and a US consumer products company (KAiBRE/KAiSDLC).
About 60% of deals won this fiscal were AI-led or largely AI-driven, per management.
Deal sizes are rising but are increasingly shorter (3-9 month) AI projects rather than multi-year annuity contracts; management said margins are not shrinking.
Competition is increasingly from well-funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and captive tech teams, not from larger listed IT peers.
Top 5, 10 and 20 clients contribute 30%, 41% and 54% of revenue. Education and Publishing is 29%, technology and consulting 20%, BFSI 19%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for AI R&D spend, and is there any plan for buybacks or M&A with the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: AI R&D stays at about INR 40-50 crore this year. Cash of INR 710 crore predates the INR 200 crore TNQTech payout, and management is in M&A dialogue but nothing has matured; no buyback was mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth consistent with the full-year guidance, given the strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained high single-digit FY27 growth guidance and cited market softness from the war and uncertainty. The CFO clarified that 43% growth refers to PAT, while revenue grew 9.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Digital Technologies grown slowly with margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to traction in KAi underwriting, KAiSDLC and KAiBRE, with legacy modernisation projects starting. It said the segment carries the AI investment, so removing it would give a much healthier margin.

qa_highlights.question: How has the competitive landscape changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not compete much with large listed IT players. Competition comes from funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and in-house tech teams.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks to the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Key risks are customers automating in-house instead of outsourcing, captive/GCC setups, and geopolitical softness.

qa_highlights.question: What is the five-year blueprint and what are the revenue drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about INR 3,000 crore over roughly three years from about INR 2,000 crore now, with organic growth from AI platforms and bolt-on acquisitions.

risks_watch: Customer insourcing to automation and GCC/captive setups could reduce outsourcing budgets, per management.
Geopolitical uncertainty (the war) is cited as softening demand; management said it needs to settle.
Shift toward shorter AI projects (3-9 months) rather than multi-year annuity deals could affect revenue visibility.
Digital Experiences declined 5.3% YoY and Digital Technologies margin is 8.9%; watch for recovery.
Whether AI R&D spend (INR 40-50 crore) remains flat next year is undecided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI-led deal wins, margins and the INR 3,000 crore ambition, but cautious on near-term demand, which management said remains soft due to the war. Management was vague on TNQTech's standalone contribution and on the FY28 AI spend.
key_quotes: So, we have projected a high single-digit growth in our guidance. We are maintaining that.
We are seeing strong market validation of our AI-first strategy.
So, a project that will take three years can be probably done in six months now.

growth.why: FY27 high single-digit revenue growth guidance was reiterated (Q1 revenue +9.9% YoY) and about 60% of FY27 deals are AI-led, but no physical capacity, utilisation or capex was discussed, and the ~INR 3,000 crore 3-year revenue target is an aspiration mixing organic and inorganic growth.
